verdict.rationale: Babylon.js is a client-side library, so the closest equivalent to an OpenAPI spec is its type definitions. The evidence implies these exist: TypeScript support with full IntelliSense, published npm packages, and a generated TypeDoc API reference, plus an llms.txt index for AI consumption. The probe confirms no OpenAPI or Swagger file exists at any candidate path. Missing for 10: an explicitly documented downloadable machine-readable spec (e.g. published .d.ts or TypeDoc JSON as a spec artifact), confirmation that type definitions ship in the npm packages, and any hands-on corroboration of agent use.
